ambiguities.readings: Ecosystem numbers (papers, downloads, awards, attendance) either fail the first layer (no driver touched) or are kept as optional; I kept as optional because 6.2 lists them.
Own-stock valuation multiples are in the 'do not keep' table but 5.3 and 6.2 say evaluation counts them optional; reject or keep-optional.
Outlet reports full production plus fall shipping: fact (already happened) or third-party view (future plan, speaker not the company).
Anonymous sources on a government decision: kind 3 (who speaks) or kind 4 (what it is).
Company says it aims to borrow, sources say at least $20B: tier by main claim is party_statement or rumour; the standard gives the example without an answer.
A headline duplicate is not recorded, but no 5.3 row names it; sentences of one event under 5.6 are one record but are classified per sentence here.
Vague benefit or praise sentences fit both the adjective-quote row and the background row.
Named customers building own chips fits class 2 ('has a name') or the known-generalization row.
Executive appointments and pay are in neither 5.1 nor 5.3; 4.3 says 'evidence or not kept'. I kept the appointment as supporting and rejected pay and role colour.
Sentence mixes a stock reaction and company's dispute of a report; I kept it for the dispute.
Rival's FDA approval: class 2 (rival's action) or class 4 (regulator decision).
Industry data as fact or third-party view; the covered company in X14 (vendor or payments company) is not given.
Total revenue: rewrite into the segment question and open (Q14) or treat as the same question (Q19); Q14 could also be refused because total revenue as written is not opened.
A tariff already extended through 2027 may be effectively settled; the standard does not ask for uncertainty, so open.
Share-of-sales and per-customer revenue might be segment-like A questions or only components of the revenue question.
A fine on one bank is a regulatory decision (E) or a litigation-type result on the closed list.
'Fuel cost per available seat mile' is a unit metric, not the fuel cost amount named in the example.
Half restates the December permission and half is new; unclear whether to split.
